name: Ali G Driving Scene AI: Grip the Blue Wheel and Head-Bang to the Drop
blurb: The Ali G driving scene AI trend puts you in the car scene from the 2002 film Ali G Indahouse: you grip a light-blue steering wheel with a dead-serious face, then head-bang hard when the bass drops.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 10 s, 720p, 9:16, sound on. The video prompt
prompts.text:
A funny car clip filmed like a real phone video, photorealistic, natural skin and natural colors, warm golden light through the windows. Not CGI, not a cartoon.

The driver is the person in [Image 1], in every frame: copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles), with the hair and the clothes from [Image 1]. So their friends recognize them at once. The face stays the same from the first frame to the last, sharp and clear in every front shot. Never morph. If [Image 1] shows an animal, the driver is that animal sitting upright in the driver's seat with its front paws on the wheel, with its own face, fur and markings, not a person.

The place: a small, old, boxy 1980s three-door hatchback with a stripped interior: a bare metal roll cage behind the front seats, black racing bucket seats with harness belts, a painted teal-green dashboard, and a small, chunky light-blue padded steering wheel; outside the windows, a quiet red-brick suburban street of semi-detached houses in warm late-afternoon sun. The car rolls slowly down the street, so the houses slide past the side windows.

The shots, cut on the beat:
1. 0-2 s: a close front view through the windscreen, the camera low on the dashboard: the driver grips the light-blue wheel with both hands and stares straight ahead with a dead-serious face while the beat builds, a tiny nod on each kick.
2. 2-4 s: the bass drops. A side view from the passenger seat: the driver head-bangs hard to the beat, fast deep nods from the neck, one hand on the wheel, the other hand rakes through the hair and flicks out.
3. 4-6.5 s: the close front view again: both hands on the wheel, the driver head-bangs hard in time with the bass, shoulders bouncing, mouth open in an amazed "ohh", the face sharp between the nods.
4. 6.5-8.5 s: the side view: the driver throws one arm out wide on the beat and rocks the whole upper body, the other hand still on the wheel.
5. 8.5-10 s: the close front view: the driver stops dead on the last beat, looks straight into the lens and points at the camera with one finger, with a slow, cool nod.

Audio: an original fast 1990s jungle and drum and bass style track: a quiet build for the first 2 seconds, then a huge, deep bass drop at 2 s that keeps pumping to the end, with the hum of a small engine under it. No dialogue, no lyrics, no singing.

Exactly one person in the car, nobody else. One steering wheel, two hands, no extra limbs. No badges, no logos, no brand names and no text anywhere: not on the wheel, the seats, the belts, the dashboard, the windscreen, the sun visor or the car. No subtitles, no watermark.
